'''Kornel Andrzej Morawiecki''' (3 May 1941 – 30 September 2019) was a [[Polish people|Polish]] politician, the founder and leader of [[Fighting Solidarity]] (Polish: ''Solidarność Walcząca''), one of the splinters of the [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]] movement in Poland during the 1980s.<ref name=Ramet/> His academic background was that of a [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]].<ref name=jprs/> He was also a member of the 8th legislature of the [[Sejm]],<ref>{{cite web | url = http://parlament2015.pkw.gov.pl/344_sejm/3_DOLNOSLASKIE_Wroclaw | title = Wybory do Sejmu i Senatu | access-date = 2015-10-27 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170703051326/http://parlament2015.pkw.gov.pl/344_Sejm/3_DOLNOSLASKIE_Wroclaw | archive-date = 2017-07-03 | url-status = dead }}</ref> of which was also the [[Senior Marshal]] on 12 November 2015. His son [[Mateusz Morawiecki]] was the [[Prime Minister of Poland|Prime Minister]] of Poland from 2017 to 2023,<ref>{{cite web|title=Komitet Polityczny PiS desygnował Mateusza Morawieckiego na Premiera|url=http://pis.org.pl/aktualnosci/komitet-polityczny-pis-desygnowal-mateusza-morawieckiego-na-premiera|website=Prawo i Sprawiedliwość|accessdate=7 December 2017}}</ref> as well as a former chairman of [[Bank Zachodni WBK]].

==Life and career==
{{Conservatism in Poland|Politicians}}
Morawiecki was born in Warsaw, Poland, the son of Michał and Jadwiga (née Szumańska). He graduated from the [[gimnazjum]] of [[Adam Mickiewicz]] in 1958 in Warsaw. He finished a higher degree in physics at the [[University of Wrocław]] in 1963. He completed his [[PhD|doctorate]] under [[Jan Rzewuski]] in [[Quantum Field Theory]] in 1970. He worked as a researcher at the [[University of Wrocław]], at first in the Institute of Physics, and later in Mathematics. After 1973, he worked at the [[Wrocław University of Technology|Wrocław Polytechnic]].

In 1968 he took part in student strikes and demonstrations.<ref>Government of the Czech Government, "August 21, 2008: Premier Awarded Commemorative Medals to Ten Dissidents from 1968", 21. 8. 2008, [http://www.vlada.cz/en/media-centrum/tiskove-zpravy/august-21--2008:-premier-awarded-commemorative-medals-to-ten-dissidents-from-1968-40255/]</ref> After the repression of the student protests, together with a group of close friends he edited, printed, and distributed pamphlets which denounced the Communist government for their repressions against the protesting students.<ref name="Obywatel">{{in lang|pl}} [http://www.obywatel.org.pl/index.php?module=subjects&func=viewpage&pageid=789  Solidarność Walcząca, czyli po niepodległość bez kompromisów] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928000105/http://www.obywatel.org.pl/index.php?module=subjects&func=viewpage&pageid=789 |date=2007-09-28 }} Magazyn Obywatel nr 5 / 2005 (25)</ref>

Since 1979, he became the editor of the [[Biuletyn Dolnośląski]] (Lower Silesian Bulletin) together with [[Jan Waszkiewicz]], an [[Polish underground press|underground newspaper]]. He was a delegate to the First National Congress of [[NSZZ Solidarity]].<ref name=jprs/>

At the end of May 1982, together with [[Paweł Falicki]], he founded the "Organization of Fighting Solidarity" which was a unique political opposition organization in Poland and the countries of the Soviet Bloc. It was the only group which from the beginning of its existence called for an end to communism in Poland<ref name=jprs>[https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA336472.pdf JPRS Report, East Europe, June 4, 1990, pgs. 18-21]</ref> and other Soviet satellites, the establishment of sovereign governments independent from Moscow therein, the breakup of the Soviet Union and separation of the USSR republics into new nation states, and the reunification of Germany within its [[Potsdam Agreement|Potsdam]]-imposed borders. While eventually all these things did in fact come to pass, at the time this program was seen as quite radical and unrealistic, even in dissident circles.

However, Fighting Solidarity also rejected the use of violence to achieve its aims.<ref name=jprs/> After the declaration of [[martial law in Poland]] in 1981, Morawiecki became one of the most wanted people in Poland.<ref name="Adamski">Artur Adamski, "Czas wielkiej próby" (The Time of Great Trial), Encyclopedia Solidarnosci (Encyclopedia of Solidarity) and Gazeta Polska, June 4, 2008, {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130416134802/http://www.encyklopedia-solidarnosci.pl/wiki/index.php?title=EWM_GP_23/2008}}</ref> In 1984, on the directive of General [[Czesław Kiszczak]], a special team was created in the [[Ministry of Interior and Administration of the Republic of Poland|Ministry of Internal Affairs]] charged with observing several dozen locations in which the authorities thought he could show up.<ref name=Adamski/>

On 9 November 1987, after six years of conspiratorial activity in the underground, he was caught and arrested by the [[Służba Bezpieczeństwa]] (Secret Police) in [[Wrocław]] and was immediately transported by helicopter to [[Warsaw]], and imprisoned in [[Rakowiecka Prison]]. Despite his capture, none of his associates, nor those who hid him during the past six years, nor the archives of the organization were captured. At the end of April 1988 he was given the opportunity to travel to Rome for much needed medical treatment by the communist authorities (who at the time were trying to get rid of "difficult" people), while his right of return to Poland was guaranteed through mediation by the [[Catholic Church]].<ref name=Ramet/> Three days later, he attempted to return to Poland but his passport was confiscated and he was deported from the airport in Warsaw to [[Vienna]].<ref name="Ramet">Sabrina P. Ramet, "Social currents in Eastern Europe", Duke University Press, 1995, pg. 98 and 190, [https://books.google.com/books?id=F3HTHpikwq4C&dq=Kornel+Morawiecki&pg=PA98], [https://books.google.com/books?id=F3HTHpikwq4C&q=Morawiecki&pg=PA98]</ref> He managed to illegally re-enter Poland in September 1988, by pretending to be a Canadian human rights delegate.<ref name=Ramet/>

After the fall of communism in Poland, Morawiecki registered his candidacy for the post of [[President of Poland]] in 1990, but in the end was unable to collect the required 100,000 signatures.<ref>Dominik Gajda, "Poland After the Round Table - The History of the Independent Poland 1989-2007", pg. 4, [http://www.gloszp.pl/Poland%20after%20the%20Round%20Table.pdf]</ref> During his televised election campaign he symbolically turned over a round table, a reference to the [[Polish Round Table Agreement]] which, he felt, compromised too much with the communists.<ref>Kornel Morawiecki, "Dlaczego przewróciłem okrągły stolik" (Why did I overturn a round table?), ''[[Rzeczpospolita (newspaper)|Rzeczpospolita]]'', 05-02-2009, [http://www.rp.pl/artykul/9133,258725_Morawiecki__Dlaczego_przewrocilem_okragly_stolik.html] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120303004634/http://www.rp.pl/artykul/9133,258725_Morawiecki__Dlaczego_przewrocilem_okragly_stolik.html|date=2012-03-03}}</ref>

For his activism in support of an independent Poland, the [[Polish Government in Exile]] under president [[Kazimierz Sabbat]] awarded him the Officer's Cross of [[Polonia Restituta]] (Order of Poland Reborn). In June 2007, on the 25th anniversary of Fighting Solidarity, he refused to accept the Grand Cross of Polonia Restituta from the President of Poland, arguing that the organization he represented deserved the highest possible state honour - the [[Order of the White Eagle (Poland)|Order of the White Eagle]].<ref name=Bart>Bartłomiej Radziejowski, "Czechów powinna przepraszać Moskwa" (Moscow Should Apologize to the Czechs), Rzeczpospolita, 2008-08-23, accessed at {{cite web |url=http://solidarni.org/wolni_i_solidarni/aktualnosci_sw/kornel_morawiecki_dla_rzeczpospolitej |title=Kornel Morawiecki dla Rzeczpospolitej - Wolni i Solidarni |accessdate=2009-08-07 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090723072217/http://www.solidarni.org/wolni_i_solidarni/aktualnosci_sw/kornel_morawiecki_dla_rzeczpospolitej |archivedate=2009-07-23 }}</ref> He was also awarded the [[Karel Kramář]] Medal by the [[Czech Prime Minister]] [[Mirek Topolánek]], for his opposition to the [[Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia]] in 1968.<ref name=Bart/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://icv.vlada.cz/scripts/detail.php?id=39588&tmplid=577|title=Výstava 21. 8. - 26. 10. 2008: Za vaši a naši svobodu - Fotogalerie - ICV|website=icv.vlada.cz|access-date=2011-05-03|archive-date=2011-07-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726001748/http://icv.vlada.cz/scripts/detail.php?id=39588&tmplid=577|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was one of the candidates in the [[2010 Polish presidential election]], but received only 0.13% of the vote and did not make it into the second round. In the [[2015 Polish parliamentary election|2015 Sejm election]], he was first-place candidate on the [[Kukiz'15]] electoral list of [[Paweł Kukiz]] in the [[Wrocław (parliamentary constituency)|Wrocław electoral district]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Wybory do Sejmu RP i Senatu RP | url=http://parlament2015.pkw.gov.pl/344_sejm/3_DOLNOSLASKIE_Wroclaw | publisher=Państwowa Komisja Wyborcza | accessdate=27 October 2015 | language=Polish | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703051326/http://parlament2015.pkw.gov.pl/344_Sejm/3_DOLNOSLASKIE_Wroclaw | archive-date=3 July 2017 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was involved in a Sejm scandal in April 2016, when Morawiecki left his Sejm member card in the voting device after feeling ill and exiting the debating hall, resulting in MP Małgorzata Zwiercan casting his vote for him. [[Civic Platform|The political party Civic Platform]] notified the [[National Public Prosecutor's Office]] of this event. Following the scandal, he left [[Kukiz'15]] and began organizing his own party along with Małgorzata Zwiercan, who had been expelled from the Parliamentary club.

Apart from his work as a politician, he also worked at the Mathematics Institute of the [[Wrocław University of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://old.im.pwr.wroc.pl/ang/visit/kmorawiecki.html|title=Kornel Morawiecki - english version|website=old.im.pwr.wroc.pl|access-date=2009-08-07|archive-date=2019-10-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001065459/http://old.im.pwr.wroc.pl/ang/visit/kmorawiecki.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1959 he married Jadwiga with whom he has four children including [[Mateusz Morawiecki]], the [[Prime Minister of Poland]]. After his divorce from Jadwiga, he married Anna with whom he had a son.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newsweek.pl/polska/mateusz-morawiecki-nowym-ministrem-rozwoju-i-wicepremierem,artykuly,373730,1.html|title=Mateusz Morawiecki nowym ministrem rozwoju i wicepremierem w rządzie Beaty Szydło|date=9 November 2015|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://dzikikraj.interia.pl/mowatrawa/news-morawiecki-ma-zone-zyje-z-partnerka,nId,1938836|title=Morawiecki: Ma żonę, żyje z partnerką|last=INTERIA.PL|publisher=|access-date=2018-01-29|archive-date=2018-03-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312042322/http://dzikikraj.interia.pl/mowatrawa/news-morawiecki-ma-zone-zyje-z-partnerka,nId,1938836|url-status=dead}}</ref> He died in 2019 from [[pancreatic cancer]].
